title: 🐘 The Mystery of the Giant Family
text: Imagine walking through a dense forest in India. Suddenly, you feel the ground shake... thud, thud, thud! You peek through the bushes and see a massive family of elephants walking together. But wait, if you look closely, you will notice something strange. Where are the adult male elephants? Why is it only females and babies in this giant group?

title: Socratic Question
text: If you had to lead a large family through a dangerous jungle to find food and water, who do you think would be the best leader? Why do you think elephant families follow the oldest female?

content.title: The Elephant Herd Structure
content.description: Visualizing an elephant herd with the Matriarch at the front leading the way.

title: The Reveal: Meet the Matriarch
text: In the world of elephants, a group is called a **Herd**. A herd mainly consists of female elephants and their babies (calves). The oldest and most experienced female elephant is the leader, known as the **Matriarch**. She knows the ancient paths and remembers where to find the best water and food, even during dry seasons!

content.definition: A large group of animals, especially hoofed mammals, that live, feed, or travel together.
A female who is the head or leader of a family or tribe.

content.question: Who is the leader of an elephant herd?

title: Reflection
text: Think about your own family. Who makes the important decisions, like where to go for a holiday or what to eat for dinner? Is there a 'Matriarch' or 'Patriarch' in your house whose experience guides everyone else?

title: Connection
text: Just like elephants, many other intelligent animals live in groups led by a dominant female, such as killer whales and honeybees! Working together and respecting the elders helps them survive in nature.

content.title: Mastery Challenge: Draw the Herd
content.text: Draw a picture of an elephant herd. Label the Matriarch walking in front, and at least two baby elephants (calves) following her safely. Write one sentence explaining why the Matriarch's memory is so important.
Male elephants usually leave the herd when they are 14-15 years old and live alone or in small bachelor groups. You can share this fun fact with students if they ask where the 'dads' are!

title: 🌿 The Giant's Appetite
text: Did you know that Nandu, a baby elephant, only weighs about 200 kilograms? That might sound heavy, but wait until he grows up! An adult elephant can eat more than 100 kilograms of leaves and twigs in a single day. That's like eating 1,000 apples for lunch!

title: Socratic Question
text: If you had to chew and eat 100 kilograms of leaves every single day, it would take a very long time! How do you think elephants manage to eat so much and still have time to sleep or play?

content.title: An Elephant's Day
content.description: A chart showing elephants spending 16 hours eating and only 2 to 4 hours sleeping.

title: The Reveal: Eat, Play, Sleep... Very Little!
text: Because they need so much food, elephants spend up to 16 hours a day just eating! With such a busy eating schedule, they don't have much time for a long sleep. An adult elephant sleeps for only **2 to 4 hours** a day. When they aren't eating, they love playing in mud and water to keep their giant bodies cool.

content.question: How many hours a day does an adult elephant typically sleep?

content.text: Students often assume that larger animals need more sleep to rest their huge bodies. In reality, large plant-eaters (herbivores) like elephants, giraffes, and horses sleep very little because they must spend almost all their time eating to get enough energy!

title: Reflection
text: If you only slept for 2 hours a day like an elephant, what would you do with all that extra time? Would you read more books, play games, or maybe just eat all day?

title: Connection
text: Elephants throw mud and water on themselves. The mud dries on their skin and acts like a natural sunscreen, protecting them from the hot sun and bug bites. This is exactly why we use sunscreen lotion before going out in the summer!

content.title: Mastery: Nandu's Diary
content.text: Imagine you are Nandu the baby elephant. Write a short diary entry describing your day. Mention how much food you saw your mother eat, how long you slept, and how much fun you had splashing in the muddy river with your cousins!
